steps.title: Prepare supplemented culture medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve basal DMEM/F12 powder in 1 L distilled water, add 2.438 g/L sodium bicarbonate, filter‑sterilize, and store at 2–8 °C for up to four weeks. Aliquot 100 mL, then add 89 mL basal medium, 10 mL fetal bovine serum, and 1 mL antibiotic‑antimycotic to obtain supplemented medium; store at 2–8 °C for up to four weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 70% ethanol solution
steps.instruction: Mix 700 mL absolute ethanol with 300 mL distilled water to make 1 L of 70 % ethanol; store at room temperature in a tightly closed container for several months.

steps.title: Seed breast cancer cells in plates
steps.instruction: Plate 1 × 10⁶ MDA‑MB‑231 cells and 1.5 × 10⁶ MCF‑7 cells per 100 × 20 mm plate in supplemented medium; incubate at 37 °C, humidified 5 % CO₂. Seed enough plates so each contains ~2 × 10⁶ cells at 70 % confluence after 24 h. Verify MCF‑7 epithelial morphology, MDA‑MB‑231 spindle shape, absence of turbidity, and cell viability >90 %.

steps.title: Harvest cells at 70% confluence
steps.instruction: When embryos reach day 8 (developed vasculature, firm CAM, reduced albumen), remove medium from each plate, wash cells twice with 5 mL PBS per plate, discard wash. Add 1 mL trypsin‑EDTA (0.25 %), incubate 37 °C 5 min, verify detachment under an inverted microscope, then add 2 mL supplemented medium.

steps.title: Count and adjust cell number
steps.instruction: Collect the cell suspension, centrifuge at 252 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 10 mL PBS, mix 1:1 with trypan blue, and count cells using a Neubauer chamber.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Transfer 3 × 10⁶ cells into a tube kept on ice, confirm viability >90 %. Centrifuge at 252 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet twice with PBS (centrifuge each wash at 252 × g for 5 min). After the final wash, remove PBS and resuspend the pellet in 30 µL cold Matrigel; keep tubes and pipette tips on ice to prevent premature polymerization.

steps.title: Polymerize Matrigel‑cell mixture
steps.instruction: Incubate the Matrigel‑cell suspension at 37 °C for 15 min to allow polymerization. Cut the tip of a 200 µL pipette with sterile scissors to facilitate aspiration of the mixture onto the egg.

steps.title: Incubate fertilized eggs for 7 days
steps.instruction: Place fertilized hen eggs in an automatic turning incubator at 37 °C and 90 % relative humidity for 7 days. Use pathogen‑free eggs with a certification; do not clean eggs with ethanol before incubation.

steps.title: Create window and expose CAM
steps.instruction: After 7 days, remove eggs, moisten a sterile gauze pad with 70 % ethanol and wipe the eggshell surface. Using forceps, cut a ~1.5 cm diameter window at the blunt (air‑sac) end. With precision jeweler’s tweezers, carefully remove the inner testaceous membrane to expose the CAM. Discard eggs with undeveloped or malformed embryos. Clean the opened eggshell surface with ethanol.

steps.title: Seal window and incubate static
steps.instruction: Seal the window with transparent adhesive tape that has been disinfected with 70 % ethanol and UV‑sterilized for 1 h. Return the eggs to a static incubator (no turning).

steps.title: Lacerate CAM and inoculate cells
steps.instruction: On day 8 (the day after opening), remove the adhesive tape and verify embryo viability. Gently lacerate the CAM at the intended site using the cut tip of a 200 µL pipette. Aspirate the polymerized Matrigel‑cell mixture and place it onto the lacerated CAM.

steps.title: Re‑seal and incubate embryos
steps.instruction: Re‑seal the window with the same ethanol‑disinfected tape and incubate eggs in a static incubator at 37 °C and 90 % relative humidity. Examine embryos daily; promptly remove any dead embryos to prevent contamination.

steps.title: Monitor tumor development
steps.instruction: Seventy‑two hours after cell placement, inspect the CAM under a stereomicroscope for tumor formation. Tumors may be allowed to grow for more than 3 days if required for downstream assays.

steps.title: Excise tumors from CAM
steps.instruction: When the experiment is complete, excise the tumor by cutting the surrounding CAM with sterile scissors.

description: Validation of protocol Experiments were conducted with n = 30–40 embryos per group across three independent biological replicates. Negative controls included embryos inoculated with Matrigel only. This protocol has undergone thorough testing and validation in our laboratory. It forms the experimental foundation of a completed manuscript titled “FAK Regulates Leptin-Induced Angiogenesis and Vasculogenic Mimicry in Breast Cancer” by Herrera Vargas, Ana Karen et al. (currently under review). The protocol is an optimized version of a previous protocol, which was used and validated in the following research article: Lazzarini et al., 2016. Las nanopartículas de oro de 20 nm inhiben la proliferación e invasión de células de carcinoma mamario humano MCF-7. Mundo nano (Figures 1–3) [33]. In comparison with the protocol described by Lazzarini et al. (2016), the present study incorporated several methodological modifications. In addition to the MCF-7 cell line, the triple-negative breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 was also employed. Tumor cell implantation was performed on day 8 of embryo incubation, rather than at earlier stages, in order to improve embryo survival. Furthermore, the CAM was gently lacerated prior to cell inoculation to facilitate tumor engraftment. Finally, the number of tumor cells implanted per embryo was increased to enhance tumor establishment and growth. In addition to its application in our laboratory, this protocol is supported by previously published studies in which the chicken CAM assay was successfully used for breast cancer research. Independent reports have demonstrated reliable tumor engraftment, growth, and vascularization using breast cancer cell lines: Ranjan et al., 2023.
